title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
topic: General Machine Learning->Unsupervised and Semi-supervised Learning
claim: With scarce paired data and abundant unpaired data, the open problem is defining a training signal for unpaired samples without known correspondences.
layout: Left-to-right: inputs, frozen encoders, embeddings, similarity matrices with a question mark
description: The figure shows a vision-language alignment setup that flows left to right. On the left are image-text inputs. Two paired examples have solid borders and double-headed arrows linking them: a cat photo with 'a cat in the grass', and a blue car with 'a blue car is driving'. Three unpaired images (dog, penguin, cake) and three unpaired captions have dashed borders. Two frozen encoders, with snowflake icons, sit in the middle, one green for vision and one blue for text. Each has a small orange trainable block marked with a flame. The encoders produce green and blue embedding bars, solid for paired and dashed for unpaired. These form a block similarity matrix on the right. Paired entries are 1 on the red diagonal and -1 off it, and cross-pair entries are -1. A large gray question mark covers the unpaired-by-unpaired block, showing that its targets are unknown.
caption: Semi-supervised vision-language alignment. We tackle the alignment of frozen unimodal encoders where paired data (red blocks) are scarce but unpaired data are abundant. The key challenge is: how to define a training signal for unpaired data when ground-truth cross-modal correspondences are missing?
abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that neural networks trained on different modalities converge toward a shared statistical model of the world. Recent work exploits this convergence by aligning frozen pretrained vision and language models with lightweight alignment layers, but typically relies on contrastive losses and millions of paired samples. In this work, we ask whether meaningful alignment can be achieved with substantially less supervision. We introduce a semi-supervised setting in which pretrained unimodal encoders are aligned using a small number of image-text pairs together with large amounts of unpaired data. To address this challenge, we propose SOTAlign, a two-stage framework that first recovers a coarse shared geometry from limited paired data using a linear teacher, and then refines the alignment on unpaired samples via an optimal-transport-based divergence that transfers relational structure without overconstraining the target space. SOTAlign effectively leverages unpaired images and text, learning robust joint embeddings across datasets and encoder pairs, and significantly outperforming supervised and semi-supervised baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/SOTAlign.
